For a script this would be enough — but /tmp is tmpfs nosuid (setuid bit stripped) and dash drops the euid anyway. Winner: a hand-built 123-byte i386 ELF (tinel.py): bytes 7,8 = EI_OSABI,EI_ABIVERSION = 0,0 so the product is 0; e_phoff = 52 is the lseek offset; phdr0.p_paddr = 0 (kernel-ignored) makes the compare 0 == 0; e_ident[9..14] hides the strings "sh\0-p\0"; the 26-byte stub at file offset 84 execve("sh", {"sh","-p",0}, 0) — a dash copy in the cwd, -p keeps euid. maze4's setuid gives euid=maze5 (visible: uid=15004 euid=15005), dash -p preserves it, cat prints A3846ZPJuH.
